newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CBA denies collusion on mortgage rate cut.
newsitem.headline: CBA denies collusion on mortgage rate cut.

text.p: Commonwealth Bank of Australia, the first big bank to cut mortgage rates after Friday's official rate cut, denied on Monday thatit had colluded with the other major banks in not passing on all of the official rate cut.

"I haven't discussed interest rates with the other banks," CBA Managing Director David Murray told Australian Broadcasting Corporation radio. "We have a very careful discipline within the bank, because we don't believe in collusion, we believe in competition," Murray said.

Anti-monopoly authority, the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission, has said it would ask the four major banks to explain why they moved so quickly to all cut their standard mortgage interest rates by 0.35 percent to 7.2 percent after the Reserve Bank of Australia cut official rates by 0.5 percentage points.
ACCC Chairman Allan Fels said it was unusual for all the banks to act the same so quickly.
Earlier Prime Minister John Howard also questioned the sameness and timing of the banks' mortgage rate moves and called for them to pass on all the rate cut.
Howard also questioned the level of competition in the banking sector.
